title: COEX Artium in Gangnam: Seoul's Theater Inside COEX Mall (Beginner's Guide)
html:
If you spend any time in Gangnam, there's a good chance you'll walk right past COEX Artium without realizing it's a theater. It's tucked into the same underground complex as COEX Mall, one of the world's largest underground shopping malls, right next to Samseong Station. For first-time visitors, it's a handy example of something very "Seoul": a full concert hall and theater hiding inside a mall, mixed in with shops, a food court, and a famous library. Here's what it actually is, what kind of shows you'll find there, and how to get there without getting lost in the mall.

What Exactly Is COEX Artium?

Photo: COEX Artium, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

COEX Artium is a performance hall built and run by COEX (the Korea International Trade Association's exhibition and convention center) inside its huge Gangnam complex. It has around 808 seats, split across a 5th-floor hall (628 seats) and a smaller 6th-floor hall (180 seats), so it can host anything from a mid-size musical to a more intimate concert or fan meeting. Since 2021, a company called Interpark Theater has run the day-to-day operation of the venue, and you may also see it listed online as "COEX Shinhan Card Artium" — Korean venues often sell "naming rights" to a sponsor, so the sign out front and the name on your ticket don't always match exactly. Don't let that confuse you; locals usually just call it "COEX Artium" or "the COEX theater."

Unlike a stand-alone theater, you don't need a ticket just to see the building. It's built into the same corridor system as COEX Mall, so you'll likely walk past the entrance anyway if you're shopping, visiting the aquarium, or heading to the library.

What Kind of Shows You'll Find There

Photo: Inside COEX Artium, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

The lineup rotates constantly, so there's no single "typical" show — it could be a musical, a classical or pop concert, a K-pop-related fan meeting, or a one-off special event, in both Korean and English depending on the production. Musicals performed here are almost always in Korean, even when the story is a famous Western one, so if you don't speak Korean, a concert or a show that's more visual (like dance) will usually be easier to enjoy than a dialogue-heavy musical. Because the schedule changes often, always check what's actually playing during your trip dates rather than assuming — the easiest way is to search "코엑스아티움" (COEX Artium) or "신한카드아티움" on Interpark Ticket, which has an English version of its site and app.

Getting There: Samseong Station to COEX Mall

Photo: Entrance area near COEX Artium, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

The full address is 513 Yeongdong-daero, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, and the easiest way in is the subway:

  • Samseong Station (Line 2), Exits 5 or 6 — walk through the underground passage toward Starfield COEX Mall and follow signs for the Artium/theater once you're inside the mall. This is the route most visitors use.
  • Bongeunsa Station (Line 9), Exit 7 — leads through ASEM Plaza into the mall, a good option if you're coming from western Seoul.
  • Cheongdam Station (Line 7), Exit 2 — also connects, but it's a longer walk (10+ minutes), so Line 2 or Line 9 is more convenient if you have a choice.

Because COEX Mall is enormous and partly underground, it's easy to get turned around once you're inside. If you get lost, the simplest fix is to look for any mall directory screen or staff member and ask for "아티움" (Artium) — that's the word on all the internal signage.

Tips for First-Time Visitors

Photo: Near COEX Artium, via Korea Tourism Organization (visitkorea.or.kr).

  • Book on Interpark Ticket ahead of time rather than hoping to buy at the door — popular concerts and musicals can sell out, especially on weekends.
  • Prices and showtimes vary by production, so there's no fixed "admission fee" like a museum — check the specific listing for your dates.
  • Arrive with extra time to find the hall inside the mall, especially the first time — 15–20 minutes earlier than you would for a stand-alone theater is a safe buffer.
  • Combine it with the rest of COEX Mall: the famous Starfield Library (floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, free to visit), COEX Aquarium, and a large food court are all a short walk away, so a show here pairs easily with a few hours of exploring before or after.
  • Parking is available on-site if you're not taking the subway, but like most of Gangnam, traffic and parking fees add up fast — the subway is simpler for most travelers.

💬 Thinking about catching a show at COEX Artium, or just curious about getting around COEX Mall? Drop a question in the comments below — happy to help!
meta_description: A beginner's guide to COEX Artium, the theater inside Seoul's COEX Mall near Samseong Station — shows, tickets, and how to get there.
